1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing across all screens.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case without italics or all-caps, and text is broken into short paragraphs rather than dense blocks.

3.why: Layouts are single-column with large inputs and buttons that remain readable and usable at mobile width.

4.why: Most instructions are brief and use plain language such as 'Save this setup secret in your authenticator now'.

5.why: Demo credentials and a pre-filled mobile number provide some examples, but no format example is shown for OTP or recovery-code entry fields.

6.why: Each step shows only a short instruction; the user is never forced to read a long block to proceed.

7.why: The authenticator secret and recovery codes are displayed as plain text without a copy button, so they must be selected or transcribed manually.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent scannable alternative is offered; the flow explicitly requires manual entry of the setup secret.

9.why: Standard email and password fields can use browser autofill, but OTP and recovery-code fields show no evidence of one-time-code or password-manager support.

10.why: Clear headings and a prominent blue primary button make the current step and main action stand out on every screen.

11.why: Each screen asks for essentially one main action (sign in, send code, verify, create secret, enable MFA, save codes, etc.).

12.why: After actions the UI states the result plainly, e.g. 'Recovery code accepted and used' and 'MFA is enabled. 8 recovery codes remain'.

13.why: Users can resend verification codes, regenerate recovery codes, and retry entry without apparent lock-out or penalty.

14.why: The only visible error ('We could not complete that request. Please try again.') does not state the specific problem or how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown timers or expiration warnings appear on any code-entry or reading step, giving generous time.
